newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - U.S. ADRs flat, Gucci stands out.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - U.S. ADRs flat, Gucci stands out.

text.p: Foreign shares in New York were largely flat on Thursday, with the standout stock luxury goods maker Gucci Group N.V, analysts said.

American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were weighed along with the larger market by the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates. That prospect arose with Thursday's reports of strong housing starts and lower-than-expected jobless claims.
"It's pretty boring across the board. In Latin America, things are pretty much following the U.S. and hunching down a bit," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

He said both Latin American ADRs and Latin American exchanges were likely to be quiet ahead of the Federal Open Market Commmittee meeting on Tuesday, where the U.S. central bank will decide on whether to raise interest rates.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian state telecommunications company Telebras was at 78-3/4, up 3/8, in early afternoon. SBC Warburg Inc initiated coverage of Telebras on Thursday with a buy rating.

Gucci rose 1-1/8 to a year high of 77-1/4 on volume of 938,200 shares. Gucci "as been a phenomenal market for a couple of weeks now," one analyst said, and has been boosted in part by general support for brand-name and luxury retailers.
Gucci also reported a record profit for 1996's first half of $69.9 million on Thursday, up from $26.4 million in the same period a year ago.
